cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella is back in the stand. Handle up, please; we store it so you can take it straight to work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Routine cleaning. The fabric needs rinsing before the handle is dried; those are separate jobs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we remove debris before closing it. Fetch a dry towel, please. I'll rinse the spokes again; it is going back in that stand properly.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 storage correction, A3 cleaning sequence and A5 debris removal make expert maintenance the cover for returning a suspiciously used umbrella.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wetness causes A3 routine-cleaning claim; B4 pondweed causes A5 repeated rinse with a relevant dry towel.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 reasonably challenge the condition of B own item, while A keeps restoring rather than explaining.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 revealing material into a more exact maintenance step and insists on proper return.

specificity.evidence: A1 umbrella for work, B2 dry weather and B4 pondweed give enough evidence to infer concealed misuse.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 towel request serves the established wet restoration rather than an arbitrary holding task.
